newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar at close on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar at close on jobs data.

text.p: Mexican stocks jumped on Wednesday, fuelled by late news of a big drop in unemployment last month.
"Unemployment figures boosted stocks, and the other fundamental reason was down to the plunge in Cetes rates," a floor trader said, referring to interest rates on government bonds.
The leading IPC share index rose 70.15 points, or 1.85 percent, to 3,867.20. Trading volume was a brisk 114.4 million.
On the broad market, 107 stocks changed hands, of which 58 gained while 31 declined.
Mexico's National Statistics Institute said open unemployment fell sharply to 4.2 percent in February from 6.3 percent 12 months ago.
Unlike developed markets, falling unemployment is not seen in Mexico as a harbinger of inflation but rather as a welcome sign of recovery after a painful economic crisis, dealers said.
Dealers said Telmex L shares, and shares listed by holding company Grupo Carso and telecom Carso Global Telecom bolstered the market.
All three have corporate links and together accounted for 48 percent of all shares traded during the session.
"Telmex took a flying leap and that hauled up the bourse. Demand was heavy and dealers switched between Telmex, Gcarso and Telecom," a floor trader said.
Gcarso gained 65 centavos (8 cents) to 45.90 pesos ($5.78), while Telecom also climbed 65 centavos (8 cents) to close at 24.40 pesos ($3.07).
Telmex ADRs, meanwhile, shrugged off weakness on Wall Street to soar 1-1/8 to a year's high of 41-5/8. Telmex also traded heavily in New York, where it was the fifth most active stock.
Telmex ended at an all-time record high in peso terms of 16.58 pesos ($2.09), 48 centavos (6 cents) up on the day and just shy of an intraday high of 16.60 pesos ($2.09).
A technical analyst noted the IPC broke resistance during the session.

"Today the bourse broke resistance at 3,850 points and could head for 3,950 points," said Jaime Fernaandez, a technical analyst at the Interacciones brokerage in Mexico City. "But we think it would get no further, as there was much quick in-and-out dealing."
